Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

mcglmgraph 0.8.5

  • summary() of a fit and mc_dag_coefficients() take method, the route of the two-stage correction, and report the route taken in two_stage_method.
  • mc_wald_graph() and mc_test_adequacy() refuse a method other than "auto" when type is not "two_stage", as mc_vcov_graph() does.
  • mc_vcov_graph(): sensitivity = "expected" is refused where it has no effect, with type other than "two_stage" or with method = "shortcut", and gives a warning when method = "auto" takes the shortcut.
  • mc_pc_skeleton() skips a conditioning set that gives no valid test, as mc_separating_sets() does, instead of stopping: the set removes no edge, and the skipped tests are counted in diagnostics$n_unusable and reported in one warning of class "mcg_unusable_tests".
  • mc_graph_pipeline() has the gate complete_separation, which fails when the skeleton search skipped a test, so such an output is not labeled a CPDAG. mc_cpdag_stability() counts those resamples in B_incomplete and reports them in one warning.

mcglmgraph 0.8.4

  • mc_test_independence() and mc_partial_cor_delta() take method, the route of the two-stage correction, as mc_vcov_graph() does.
  • method = "auto" of the two-stage correction takes the full form, when it is available, for a fit in which a response has a variance function other than "constant". Every function that uses the two-stage variance follows it; method = "shortcut" gives the shortcut for such a fit.
  • mc_partial_cor_delta(): the rows of the "gradient" attribute for pairs outside the support hold 0, the gradient of a constant, instead of NA.
  • mc_wald_graph() refuses a contrast whose variance is at most 1e-6 of its model-based variance, which covers a parameter the first stage fixes under either route of the two-stage variance.

mcglmgraph 0.8.3

  • mc_spd_line_search(): the default max_halvings is 30, the value mcglm_graph() uses internally.
  • mc_partial_cor_delta(): a pair outside the specified support (an absent GGM edge, or a pair outside the moral graph of a DAG) returns pcor = 0 and NA for se, statistic, p_value, lower and upper, and its row of the "gradient" attribute is NA. Rows of present pairs are unchanged.
  • mc_partial_cor_delta(): a pair whose partial correlation is undefined (a nonpositive product of precision diagonals) returns NA in pcor and in the inference columns instead of 0. A variance that is negative beyond rounding, because the covariance of the parameters is not positive semidefinite, gives NA rather than 0.
  • Renamed, with no alias: the attribute centre of mc_vcov_graph(type = "two_stage") is now center, and the column prop_centre of the v-structure tables of mc_find_vstructures() and mc_graph_pipeline() is now prop_center.

mcglmgraph 0.8.2

  • coef() on an mcglm_graph object accepts the type values of coef.mcglm() ("beta", "tau", "power", "correlation"), so summary() prints the first-stage tables before the graph layer and anova() works. A failure of the first-stage summary raises a warning.

  • mc_graph_bootstrap(), mc_graph_stability(refit = "full") and mc_cpdag_stability(refit = "full") return, in every resample, the first stage refitted on that resample. A statistic that reads the regression or dispersion parameters gets their bootstrap spread.

  • A refit of the graph layer on a resample or on another support refreshes every convergence and conditioning diagnostic of the $graph block.

  • mc_select_lambda() and mc_graph_penalized(): supports from independent and warm-started grids can differ for pairs near the penalty threshold, since certified solutions agree only up to the tolerance.

  • mc_graph_penalized() accepts a step when the sufficient-decrease condition of Beck and Teboulle (2009) holds, so the penalized objective does not increase and the iteration reaches its parameter tolerance along the grid of mc_select_lambda() and the path of mc_graph_stability(q = ).

  • mc_select_lambda() takes max_iter, tol and kkt_tol and passes them to the penalized fit of every grid point.

  • The support of a penalized fit is the set of edge coefficients that are not exactly zero.

  • mcglm_graph() warns when the graph layer did not converge, and says so when the number of units does not exceed the number of responses.

  • mc_wald_graph(), and with it mc_test_independence() and mc_test_adequacy(), refuses a contrast whose covariance is singular on its range, such as a parameter the first stage fixes under type = "two_stage".

  • A response transformed on the left side of its formula, as log(y) ~ x, is accepted and labeled by its expression.

  • An identity within-response structure stored as a sparse matrix is recognized at any size.

  • mc_graph_stability() checks criterion on entry.

  • The examples generate their data with base R.

  • summary() returns an object of class "summary.mcglm_graph" with a print method, takes variability for the standard errors of the graph parameters and shows the status of a graph layer that did not converge.

  • mc_partial_cor_delta() takes interval = "fisher" and mc_dag_coefficients() takes r2_interval = "logit", for bounds that stay inside the range of the quantity.

  • mc_edge_scores() computes only the block asked for in which, and the efficient score of an absent edge in closed form, which shortens mc_graph_stepwise().

  • mc_plot_network() stops each arrow of a DAG at the border of its node, so the direction is visible, and bounds the edge width.

  • The skeleton and the enumeration of separating sets apply one kernel for the conditional-association test, which refuses a block of the covariance that is not positive definite.

mcglmgraph 0.8.1

  • mc_vcov_graph(type = "two_stage", method = "full") with the default sensitivity = "observed" differentiates the first-stage equations as mcglm solved them, with its bias correction when the fit used it. Standard errors of parameters the first stage nearly fixes, such as the innovation variance of a root node, match their sampling spread.
  • The two-stage shortcut divides the propagation factor of each response by its average squared Pearson residual, the value the first stage fixes. A parameter the first stage fixes exactly gets a zero standard error, and where the shortcut is exact it matches the full form with the observed sensitivity.
  • The two-stage shortcut is offered only when the prior weights are constant; otherwise method = "auto" takes the full form and method = "shortcut" is refused.
  • The help page of mc_vcov_graph() states when sensitivity = "expected" can be far off and recommends the observed sensitivity.

mcglmgraph 0.8.0

  • mc_between_graph() stores the edges in canonical order (i < j, rows sorted), the order of the edge parameters. Edge scores, Wald statistics and the candidates ranked by mc_graph_stepwise(direction = "forward") or "both" do not depend on the order in which the edges are supplied, and a pair given as (j, i) is accepted.
  • The DAG layer fits the empty support, edges = matrix(0L, 0, 2), with delta_j = S_jj for every response; print, summary, the covariances, mc_dag_coefficients() and the criteria handle it.
  • A near-singular parent block in the closed-form DAG root (reciprocal condition number of the block rescaled to a unit diagonal at or below rcond_tol) is reported in status, which names the affected responses, and the fit is not certified for inference. The GES local score refuses such a parent set. The test, the fallback ridge and the innovation-variance floor are relative to the scale of each response, so the root is equivariant to a rescaling of the responses.
  • mcglm_graph() refuses missing or non-finite responses, missing covariates and non-finite offset, weights or Ntrial values with an error naming the response and the number of rows, and refuses a fit whose Pearson residuals are not finite; complete cases are required.
  • The Wald statistic of an edge whose estimated variance is not positive is NA instead of 0, and mc_graph_stepwise() does not take that edge as the weakest one; it warns instead.
  • method = "auto" of the two-stage correction, on a DAG with an immorality (where the shortcut is only first-order for the parameters of the collider and its descendants), takes the full form when it is available and, when it is not, the shortcut with a warning. Other fits keep their route.

mcglmgraph 0.7.0

  • mc_graph_penalized(), mc_select_lambda() and stability selection refuse, with a clear error, a response whose Pearson residuals have no variance: the diagonal start and the largest penalty of the path require S_kk > 0 for every response. Previously the start held an infinite parameter and the failure surfaced later as a decomposition or convergence error.
  • Documentation: mc_vcov_graph(), mc_dag_sensitivity() and mc_dag_coefficients() name the curvature of the empirical forms uniformly as the observed Hessian of the working criterion. No computation changed.

mcglmgraph 0.6.1

  • For a sparse DAG, the empirical sandwich, full and shortcut two-stage covariances, and Godambe penalties now use the observed negative Hessian of the residual working criterion. The model-based Pearson Gram matrix remains available in fitgraphgraphJ and is still used by Fisher scoring and the model-based covariance. With misspecified second moments, the observed parent block uses the residual sample covariance rather than the covariance implied by the DAG. Point estimates and the GGM computations are unchanged.
  • QIC and GBIC can aggregate Pearson scores by independent cluster through cluster and small_sample in mc_compute_criterion(), mc_graph_stepwise() and mc_select_lambda(). BIC, GBIC and EBIC use the number of independent clusters in their logarithmic penalty when cluster is supplied. Existing calls retain their previous defaults.
  • The documentation now states that the QIC optimism derivation assumes a genuinely known first stage. Same-sample estimation of marginal parameters needs an additional joint expansion. It also states the per-unit or per-cluster score-centering condition for empirical Godambe variability; aggregate centering alone does not make that variability consistent. These statistical conditions cannot be certified from a fitted object.
  • A regression test compares the sparse-DAG Hessian to numerical differentiation under deliberate covariance misspecification and checks its use in empirical sandwich, two-stage covariance and criteria.

mcglmgraph 0.6.0

The correction for the first stage reaches every fit, the tests of the graph layer take any contrast, and the documentation says under which conditions each result holds. The default routes return what 0.5.1 returned.

The full two-stage correction

  • mc_vcov_graph(type = "two_stage") gains method = c("auto", "shortcut", "full"). The full form rebuilds the first stage at its estimate with the routines of mcglm, splits its quasi-score and Pearson functions over units, and forms the two-stage influence function H^-1 (psi_2 - B A^-1 psi_1), with B by the chain rule on the Pearson residual and no condition on the mean or on the residual covariance. It covers what the shortcut refuses: a Poisson-Tweedie power that is estimated, more than one covariance component, and within-response structures that are not the identity. "auto" takes the shortcut where it applies, so a number computed before is computed again.
  • The sensitivity of the first stage is the observed one by default, the Jacobian of its estimating functions at the estimate by central differences of their totals, rebuilt with mcglm; sensitivity = "expected" takes the model-based form instead. The two agree when the first stage is correctly specified, and only the observed one keeps the correction right when it is not: on a gamma design whose third response misses a covariate, the corrected standard errors stay within 5% of the sampling spread with it and drift by up to 20% without it. The observed form inherits the conditioning of the first stage: on a weakly identified Poisson-Tweedie fit it can inflate the correction several times, which is why the attribute sensitivity_rcond reports it.
  • Either way the block of the covariance parameters on the regression parameters is kept. The joint_inv_sensitivity that mcglm reports sets it to zero, because the covariance it builds at the end of the fit carries no derivative in the means. That block is not zero when the variance depends on the mean, and without it the regression part of the first stage stops cancelling: on a gamma design with n = 20000 the diagonal coefficients come out 56% to 99% too wide. With it, the full form and the shortcut agree to 1e-4 wherever both apply.
  • With a structure that is not the identity the units are the clusters, which have to nest it: every matrix of the matrix linear predictor must vanish between distinct clusters, and that is checked.
  • mc_two_stage_available() reports both routes, shortcut_ok and full_ok with their reasons, and the one "auto" takes. ok and why keep their meaning, the shortcut’s.
  • Checked against the definitions: the unit contributions, the sensitivity and B by numDeriv, the power columns included. Checked against the sampling spread: on 400 replicates of a clustered count design, with random-effect blocks nested in 40 clusters, the full-form standard errors are 0.92 to 0.99 of the Monte Carlo deviation, where the naive sandwich is up to 2.2 times off; with an estimated Poisson-Tweedie power, 0.90 to 0.99 against 3.7 to 5.4.

Resampling by clusters

  • mc_graph_bootstrap(), mc_cpdag_stability() and mc_graph_stability(refit = "full") refit both stages for structures that are not the identity when cluster is given. Each drawn cluster keeps its own block of the structure, and a cluster drawn twice gives two blocks that do not touch, where the submatrix of the rows drawn would have joined the copies. Without cluster such a fit is refused, and the message no longer suggests cluster where it could not help.
  • mc_graph_stability() takes cluster and then draws half of the clusters.

Tests of the graph layer

  • mc_wald_graph() tests any linear hypothesis L theta = c on the graph parameters, with the three covariances, degrees of freedom equal to the rank of L and a refusal of a right-hand side that redundant rows contradict.
  • mc_test_adequacy() refits the saturated graph on the same residuals and tests the omitted edges jointly, and marks the result as descriptive when the support was selected on the same data.
  • mc_test_independence() is mc_wald_graph() with the contrast that selects every edge, gains type, and returns the same statistic to the last bit.

Residual degrees of freedom

  • mc_residual_df() returns nu_e = n - h in the exact case, every response Gaussian with identity link, constant variance and a common design of rank h, and says why otherwise. The separation routines take df_residual = "auto" where a fit is at hand and refuse a fit for which it is not exact. The default remains the approximation by n; with the intercept alone the two coincide.

Directed layer

  • mc_dag_coefficients() gives intervals for the standardized coefficient and for R^2 by the delta method, with analytical gradients through Sigma_b. That is the new default, interval = "delta"; "fixed_factor" keeps the interval of 0.5.1, which carried the variances in the factor as if known.

The L1 path and stability selection

  • mc_select_lambda() takes warm_start and include_zero, and mc_graph_penalized() takes start.
  • mc_compute_criterion() and the selectors accept "ebic", the extended BIC of Foygel and Drton, with ebic_gamma.
  • mc_graph_stability() takes q: every subsample selects the first q edges along the L1 path, and the bound of Meinshausen and Buehlmann on the expected number of false edges is reported. sampling = "complementary" draws the pairs of Shah and Samworth.
  • The L1 iteration starts from the diagonal fit of the empty graph and does not stop at a small step while the KKT residual fails. The certified solutions do not change.

Documentation

  • The conditions under which the first stage acts as a diagonal rescaling, a correctly specified mean and a residual covariance that does not depend on the covariates, are stated where the package relies on them, and so is what the checks of a fit cannot verify.
  • mc_graph_stepwise() refuses a directed fit instead of converting it.
  • The small-sample flag of mc_vcov_graph() says whether G/(G-1) was applied.

mcglmgraph 0.5.1

A one-line correction with a disproportionate effect, and the test that pins it.

  • .is_identity_structure() read the dimension of a within-response structure through dim(). Matrix sits in Imports, so in a session that had not yet attached it the S4 method was not dispatched and dim() answered NULL on the ddiMatrix the first stage builds, which sent the function down its FALSE branch before it could reach the ddiMatrix case written for exactly that object. The dimension and the unit-diagonal flag are now read from the slots with attr(), which needs no namespace. Nothing else changes, and no dependency is added.
  • What it fixed for the user. mc_graph_stability(refit = "full") stopped on the first call of a session, with a message about a matrix linear predictor that resampling would not preserve, and succeeded on the second call with the same input. mc_two_stage_available() reported a spurious extra reason on the first call. Both came from the same line.
  • A regression test runs the check in a fresh process through callr, since any earlier call in the same session loads the namespace and hides the fault.

mcglmgraph 0.5.0

Three additions. Nothing that existed changes: the default fitting route, the skeleton search and the standard orientation rule return exactly what 0.4.0 returned, and the test suite pins that.

Inference on the graph layer

  • mc_vcov_graph() exports the covariance of the graph parameters in its two forms, the model-based J_n^-1 and the sandwich J_n^-1 V_n J_n^-1, with clustering and the small-sample factor. The sandwich was only reachable through an internal function, so a reported standard error could not be reproduced from the public interface. mc_test_independence() now consumes this very matrix, so the accessor and the test cannot drift apart.
  • The sandwich uses the conditioning tolerance the fit was solved under, instead of the default. It could otherwise accept a sensitivity the fitting engine had refused, or refuse one it had accepted.

Order-independent orientation

  • mc_separating_sets() enumerates every set that separates a pair of responses on a given skeleton, with the partial correlation and the p-value of each. The skeleton search records only the first such set, which is all the standard rule needs; two sets can separate the same pair with very different strength, and which one is kept is decided by the order of enumeration.
  • mc_graph_pipeline() and mc_find_vstructures() take orient_rule, with the conservative rule of Ramsey, Zhang and Spirtes (2006) and the majority rule of Colombo and Maathuis (2014) beside the standard one. Combined with the order-independent skeleton the package already used, they make the whole procedure independent of the labeling of the responses. Both are native and use the same conditional-association test and the same degrees-of-freedom contract as the skeleton, so a difference between two runs is attributable to the rule and not to a change of test.
  • mc_orient_meek() takes ambiguous. A triple that a rule leaves undecided withholds R1 and R3 where they would settle it by propagation. R2 forbids a cycle and involves no unshielded triple, so it is unaffected.
  • On a chain whose extremes have marginal correlation small enough for the order-zero test to accept, the standard rule declares a collider that does not exist, and the two new rules leave the triple unoriented.

The unit-diagonal constraint

  • mc_dag_unit_diagonal() returns the innovation variances under which the covariance of the directed layer is a correlation matrix, and says whether the coefficients admit them. The undirected layer fixes its diagonal at one at the cost of nothing; here the constraint confines the coefficients to the open set where every innovation variance stays positive, defined by as many nonlinear inequalities as there are responses. The set contains the origin and is a proper subset whenever there is an edge, which is why the fitting routines do not impose it. It also carries the rescaling to the one representative of the orbit with unit innovations.

Two gates in C++

  • The check for a directed cycle and the Dor and Tarsi check for a consistent extension are combinatorics on the adjacency, with no floating point in them, and both are evaluated once per resample by the structure-frequency routines. They moved to C++, and agree with the plain-R versions on 300 random partially directed graphs.
  • Two pieces stay in R on purpose. The per-unit Pearson contributions were already reassociated into one BLAS call per parameter, and sit on the path that decides every selection: moving them would buy little and risk changing a criterion in its last bit, which is enough to flip an edge at a tie. The conditional-association test and the loop of the skeleton search stay for the same reason.

Greedy equivalence search, native

  • mc_ges() searches over Markov equivalence classes by the two-phase procedure of Chickering: a forward phase from the empty class applying the insertion that raises the score most, then a backward phase applying the best deletion. No external library is involved. It answers the same question as mc_graph_pipeline() by other means: one trades every edge against a penalty and never tests a hypothesis, the other tests separations at a fixed level and then orients, and the two need not agree.
  • The search is well posed only because the working criterion is score equivalent, two members of a class fitting the same covariance with the same parameter count. The test suite checks that on enumerated classes before checking anything else.
  • The operators, the local scores and the extension of a partially directed graph to a DAG are in C++. Each operator’s result is mapped back to a CPDAG, so the search never leaves the space it is defined on.
  • On thirty random DAGs with n = 3000, the search recovers the true class in 23 cases against 22 for the constraint-based route.

Structural intervention distance

  • mc_sid() counts the ordered pairs of responses for which the estimated graph would send one to the wrong adjustment set. The Hamming distance counts the edges two graphs disagree about and says nothing about what the disagreement costs; two estimates at the same Hamming distance can still give the right adjustment set for every pair or for none. The SID package is not a dependency: the distance is native, with d-separation decided by ancestral moralization in C++.
  • A partially directed estimate gives an interval rather than a number, over the members of its class, which is what a CPDAG admits. The members come from mc_class_members().
  • Validity is decided by the generalized adjustment criterion and not by the back-door one. The back-door criterion is sufficient and not necessary: it refuses any set containing a descendant of the treatment, while a descendant lying on no causal path to the response does no harm. The difference is not cosmetic. Under the back-door reading the distance counted pairs the adjustment in fact recovers; under the generalized one, on 1992 pairs of random graphs, the count agrees exactly, in both directions, with whether the population regression returns the total causal effect.

What a class identifies, and what it does not

  • mc_class_members() enumerates the DAGs a CPDAG stands for, by orienting one undirected edge at a time, propagating with Meek’s rules, and abandoning a branch as soon as it creates a cycle or an immorality the class does not have. No member is produced twice, since the two branches fix opposite directions on the same edge.
  • mc_class_coefficients() fits the directed layer on the residual covariance under every member and reports, per arc, the range the class allows and whether the head is free of undirected edges, which is the condition under which a single value can be reported at all. In a five-response example with two members, the compelled arc takes 0.700 in one member and 0.431 in the other, and its sibling 0.500 against 0.780, with the closed form (g - c h) / (1 + c^2) matching.
  • Every member is checked to fit the same covariance, which is the property that makes the class, and not the DAG, what second moments identify.

Out-of-sample comparison

  • mc_graph_cv() splits the units into folds, fits the graph layer outside each fold and scores it inside, so candidate supports are compared without a penalty term and without scoring a support on the sample that chose it. What is scored is the Gaussian working criterion per held-out unit, on the scale of a log density, so differences are comparable across fold sizes.

Structure metrics inside the package

  • mc_structure_metrics() compares an estimated graph with a known one: true and false positive rates, precision, F1 and structural Hamming distance. mc_cpdag_metrics() does the same for CPDAGs (CPDAG distance, skeleton F1 and SHD, v-structure recall and precision), and mc_true_cpdag() returns the CPDAG of a known precision matrix.
  • The measures keep apart what the skeleton recovers and what the orientation does, and a rate whose denominator is empty is NA rather than a number: precision is undefined when nothing was selected, recall when there was nothing to find, over-orientation when the truth directs every edge.
  • The pair states, the v-structures and the confusion counts are in C++.

Frequencies over resamples

  • mc_graph_stability() gains refit = "full", which draws each half-sample from the rows of the data and refits the first stage on it, so the selection frequencies carry the variability of both stages. The default stays "residual", which resamples the stored residuals with the first stage held fixed and is what earlier versions did, so a recorded result keeps reproducing.
  • mc_cpdag_stability() records, for every pair of responses, how often the pair came out absent, undirected, or directed each way. An orientation the data barely support shows up as a pair whose two directions split the frequency, which a single run cannot reveal. It carries background knowledge and the orientation rule through to every resample, and reports the share of outputs that passed the validity gates and the average number of ambiguous triples.
  • Units are drawn with replacement there, keeping the sample size, which is the bootstrap convention; the selection frequencies keep half-samples, the convention of the stability-selection literature. The difference is stated in both help pages rather than left to be inferred.

Resampling both stages

  • mc_graph_bootstrap() resamples units, or whole clusters, and refits the first-stage MCGLM and the graph layer in every resample. Nothing in the package resampled the first stage before: mc_graph_stability() reuses the stored residuals, which is the comparison and not the propagation. The support of the graph is held fixed, so this is an inferential check on a given structure and not a post-selection estimator.
  • It is the route for the fits the analytical shortcut refuses, the Poisson-Tweedie ones with an estimated power among them, and it is the yardstick the shortcut is checked against. On a Gaussian design the bootstrap standard errors track type = "two_stage" and depart from the naive sandwich exactly on the diagonal coefficients, in the direction and by the amount the closed form predicts. With stage = "residual" it resamples the residuals alone and reproduces the naive sandwich, which is what isolates the contribution of the first stage.
  • The first-stage call is rebuilt from the fitted object, so a fit whose within-response structure is not the identity is refused rather than resampled in a way that would not preserve it.
  • The resamples are drawn in the parent before any dispatch, so a given seed yields the same resamples at any worker count.

A parameter vector that is a vector

  • The parameter block of a GGM fit was a one-column matrix, because that is what the line search returns, while that of a DAG fit was a plain vector. coef(fit, type = "graph") inherited the difference. Both are vectors now.

Propagating the first stage

  • mc_vcov_graph(type = "two_stage") corrects the variance of the graph parameters for the estimation of the residuals. Stacking the two sets of estimating functions gives a block triangular sensitivity whose inversion gives the influence function of the second stage; the cross sensitivity factorizes as B = Q Ubar with Q[d, r] = -(1/2) [Z_d Sigma_b](r, r), and when every response carries a single dispersion parameter that multiplies its variance function the correction needs second-stage quantities only. Until now the package reported the two conditional forms and nothing else.
  • mc_two_stage_available() says whether a fit qualifies and, when it does not, why. A fit that does not qualify raises an error rather than returning the uncorrected matrix under the corrected name. Poisson-Tweedie is additive in its dispersion parameter and qualifies only with the power fixed at one.
  • What the correction reaches is checked rather than asserted. The test suite rebuilds Q from the canonical directions of the precision, verifies that H^-1 Q[, r] is the derivative of the parameters along the diagonal rescaling of the precision, by finite differences, and that the gradients of the partial correlations annihilate it, which is why those are unaffected. With Gaussian residuals the ratio of corrected to naive standard error of a diagonal coefficient matches its closed form sqrt(2 (K_kk - 1) / K_kk), and the correction to an absent edge vanishes.
  • The per-unit Pearson contributions were split out of the empirical variability, so the correction and the sandwich share one piece of arithmetic rather than two copies of it.

Background knowledge on the orientation

  • mc_orient_meek() gains Meek’s fourth rule and the arguments required and forbidden. R1 to R3 are complete when the only oriented edges are those of the v-structures, which is why the CPDAG of a class never needed R4; it becomes necessary the moment edges are oriented from outside, because the graph is then no longer the CPDAG of any class. Adding it changes nothing without background knowledge: the CPDAG is a fixed point of the four rules, and the test suite checks that on random classes.
  • mc_graph_pipeline() takes the same two arguments, by response name or by index, and reports what was imposed. With knowledge the output is no longer the CPDAG of an equivalence class but the maximally oriented graph, the union of the members of the class that satisfy the knowledge, and the label says so. Knowledge that contradicts a compelled edge, itself, or the skeleton is refused rather than silently dropped.
  • The rules are checked against their definition and not against a second implementation: for random DAGs the test suite enumerates every orientation of the skeleton, keeps those Markov equivalent to the original that satisfy the knowledge, and requires the union to be exactly what the rules return.
  • The four rules moved to C++. R4 adds a search over pairs, which would have made a sweep cost the fourth power of the number of responses in R.

Closed-form directed layer

  • mc_dag_closed_root() solves the Pearson equations of the directed layer node by node. With directed = TRUE the arcs are read as parent and child, any acyclic set is accepted and a compatible ordering is derived, which is what fitting an estimated DAG requires.
  • mc_dag_sensitivity() assembles the sensitivity from its block form, one block per node, instead of forming P^2 traces of R x R products.
  • mcglm_graph() takes that route by default for the directed layer, including a blockwise inverse of the sensitivity. It solves the same equations exactly: on the cases in the test suite the two routes agree to 1e-15 in the parameters and in their variance, and the closed route is about forty times faster at ten responses or more. control = list(dag_solver = "newton") restores the scoring iteration. A fit taken by the closed route reports status = "closed_form" instead of "converged", since it took no step whose size a convergence rule could read; what certifies it is the score gate, which it passes by construction.
  • mc_dag_coefficients() reports the scale-free quantities, the standardized coefficient and the proportion of variance accounted for by the parents, which are the ones invariant to the diagonal rescaling the first stage induces. The raw coefficients were all the package exposed.

Documentation

  • The edge matrix is sorted lexicographically before use and gamma is read in that sorted order, not in the order the rows were supplied. That was the behavior and it was not written down.

mcglmgraph 0.4.0

Performance release. Nothing in the statistical contract changes: every result below is the same arithmetic, reassociated, and the parallel routines return exactly what the sequential ones return for a given seed.

Faster

  • The empirical variability of the estimating functions used to evaluate its quadratic form one observation at a time, inside a double loop over n and the parameter count: one BLAS call per row of data. Written as one matrix product per parameter it costs O(n R^2) in a single call. Measured 31x to 45x on the sizes this package is used at, agreeing to about 1e-14. It sits on the critical path of every Godambe-adjusted criterion, so the stepwise search under GBIC and the L1 path both inherit the gain: stability selection with ten responses, n = 500 and B = 60 went from 234.5 s to 63.9 s sequentially.

Parallel, opt-in

  • mc_graph_stability() and mc_select_lambda() accept workers. The same case above runs in 10.1 s with sixteen workers, twenty-three times the original. Both default to workers = 1.
  • The default is deliberate. A simulation study usually parallelizes at the level of the simulation cell, and a second level of workers underneath oversubscribes the machine. Inside a PSOCK worker the argument is ignored with a warning, so the nesting cannot happen by accident.
  • Reproducibility is preserved by construction: every subsample is drawn in the parent before any dispatch, so a given seed yields the same subsamples at any worker count and workers = 16 returns exactly what workers = 1 returns. Forking is used where available; Windows falls back to sequential.

mcglmgraph 0.3.4

The strict input contract introduced in 0.3.3 covered only the low-level LDL wrappers; the path that mcglm_graph() actually takes reached the kernels through separate, permissive helpers. A non-integer edge index was silently truncated there, so a caller could ask for one edge and be fitted another with no signal. There is now a single validator.

Corrections

  • .validate_edges() is the one edge contract of the package. mc_precision_bases(), mc_between_graph(), the LDL wrappers and the fitting path all funnel through it, so the same malformed input is refused the same way whichever door it came through. Non-integer, non-finite, out-of-range, self-looping and duplicated edges are errors, not silent coercions.
  • The GGM layer no longer deduplicates edges silently: a repeated pair does not define a second parameter, so it is rejected rather than dropped. This matches the behavior the DAG layer already had.
  • mc_precision_bases() validates R as a single positive integer instead of coercing it, which turned 2.7 into 2 and a length-two vector into an internal condition-length error.
  • mc_between_graph() validates at construction time and rejects ordering when type = "ggm": the precision support is unordered, and the argument was previously accepted and ignored without warning.

Documentation

  • mc_graph_penalized() states that the regularization path is always built over the complete graph, whatever support the supplied fit carries.

mcglmgraph 0.3.3

This release strengthens low-level validation, graph semantics, convergence diagnostics and reproducibility contracts.

Corrections

  • DAG partial-correlation support follows concentration/moral support instead of equating absence of a directed arc with a structural zero.
  • The LDL API rejects duplicated edges, inconsistent dimensions, non-finite values and non-positive innovation variances before entering C++ kernels.
  • CPDAG helpers distinguish internal consistency from certification of an essential graph, use an explicit residual-degrees-of-freedom contract and expose regularization or insufficient-degrees-of-freedom states.
  • Optional score-based orientation returns fields that describe the same graph, while retaining the PC skeleton separately for inspection.
  • Inference and post-selection objects expose, recompute or invalidate numerical diagnostics rather than silently carrying stale values.
  • The unused preconditioned proximal-Newton C++ kernel was removed; the public penalized route remains the Euclidean ISTA implementation certified by the parameter-change and KKT gates.
  • Gaussian-copula documentation now requires an explicit latent-scale step; inversion of observed Pearson covariance is not presented as sufficient.

New features

  • mcglmgraph() is now a second name for mcglm_graph(), spelled the way the package itself is. It is not a wrapper: the new name is bound to the existing object, so there is no forwarding layer and no way for the two spellings to drift apart. Neither name is deprecated, and the documentation is shared. The class of the returned object remains "mcglm_graph" under both spellings, because that is the identifier recorded inside saved fits and the one the S3 methods are registered on.

  • mc_partial_cor_delta() adds standard errors, Wald statistics, p-values and confidence intervals to the between-response partial correlations, by the delta method. The gradient has a closed form and the variance is the quadratic form g' V g. mc_partial_cor() returns the point estimate only.

    • variability = "model" uses J^-1; "empirical" uses the sandwich form J^-1 (n Vhat) J^-1.
    • It applies to both layers. The precision derivatives are obtained from Kdot_d = -K Sigmadot_d K, an identity that in the GGM layer returns exactly the canonical base Z_d of the statement, and in the DAG layer supplies the directions in (gamma, delta) without changing the formula.
    • Pairs outside the support are structural zeros: the gradient vanishes and the standard error is exactly zero, flagged by present = FALSE.
    • The documentation states the scope: the variance is conditional on the estimated residuals and does not propagate first-stage uncertainty; applied to a support chosen by search, it remains descriptive.

  • New RcppArmadillo kernel cpp_pcor_delta().

Tests

The analytical, numerical and graph-contract suites include adversarial cases.

  • Numerical verification of the analytical derivatives is no longer spot checking. test-analytic-derivatives.R sweeps every coordinate of both layers, in three configurations of dimension and support each: complete GGM with three responses, chain with four and sparse with five; complete DAG with three, chain with four and hub with five. Previously a single coordinate per layer was checked, which would let through a sign error confined to a diagonal base or to one specific edge orientation.
  • The estimating function is now checked against the numerical gradient of the Gaussian working criterion, in both layers, with Shat different from Sigma so that the gradient is not trivially zero.
  • The sensitivity is now checked against minus the numerical Jacobian of the estimating function, evaluated at the point where Shat coincides with the fitted covariance, which is where the identity holds exactly.
  • Structural tests of the derivatives: the GGM diagonal derivatives are rank one and negative semidefinite; the delta derivatives of the DAG layer are rank one and positive semidefinite.
  • The saturated equivalence between the GGM and DAG layers gained a unit test.
  • tests/testthat/setup.R collects the configurations and the numerical-differentiation helpers.

mcglmgraph 0.3.2

This version fixes public contracts that promised more formal validity than the procedures delivered.

  • mc_graph_pipeline() no longer labels its output as a CPDAG unconditionally. Orientation by v-structures now collects the requirements before writing them: when two colliders demand opposite directions on the same edge, neither orientation is applied and the conflict is recorded. The output is submitted to four gates: absence of conflict, acyclicity, preservation of the written colliders, and existence of a consistent DAG extension, exposed in $gates, $valid_cpdag and $label. If any gate fails, the object is called a second-order partially directed structure.
  • mc_edge_scores() now scores absent edges by the efficient score, which projects out the nuisance parameters, instead of dividing psi_e^2 by J_ee. Under the working identity the variance is the Schur complement J_ee - J_el J_ll^-1 J_le; the argument variability = "empirical" uses the fourth-order variability. The previous statistic remains in stat_unadjusted, without chi-squared calibration.
  • mc_graph_penalized(precondition = TRUE) was disabled. The preconditioned step is not the proximal operator in the metric of J and could declare convergence while violating the KKT conditions; on a chain with R = 6, n = 80 and lambda = 5 it returned an empty graph with a KKT residual close to 30.
  • Convergence of the L1 route now requires a double tolerance: relative change in the parameters and KKT residual per unit. The fields kkt, kkt_unit and kkt_tol accompany the fit, and the kkt_not_certified state distinguishes stopping by stability from stopping by stationarity.
  • The graph-layer fit records score_norm, score_norm_unit, rcond_J and stopping_rule, so that a stopping rule based on parameter change can be checked against the score norm it leaves behind.
  • mc_compute_criterion() no longer silently turns GBIC into BIC when the inversion of the sensitivity fails. The fallback is graded (exact solve, documented spectral pseudo-inverse, and only then parameter counting) and travels in the criterion_status attribute, alongside effective_dimension.
  • mc_pc_skeleton() and mc_graph_pipeline() accept df_residual, the effective sample size used in the degrees of freedom of the Fisher approximation.
  • A complete worked example of the workflow is a regression test.

mcglmgraph 0.3.1

  • The stepwise search and the penalty selection explicitly discard candidates that did not converge or whose criterion is not finite, and record the failures.
  • Frequency aggregation distinguishes attempted, valid and failed resamples, using the valid ones as the primary denominator and preserving a conservative frequency over all attempts.
  • DAG initialization deterministically regularizes singular sample covariances and records the magnitude of the spectral adjustment.
  • Fit objects propagate state, iterations and convergence metadata.

mcglmgraph 0.3.0

  • The gbic criterion now explicitly names the working BIC adjusted by the Godambe dimension. The name clbic remains as a legacy synonym.
  • Penalized estimation now accepts an iteration only when the precision is positive definite and the penalized objective does not increase. The return value includes the convergence state and the objective trajectory.
  • mc_graph_stability() is documented as a diagnostic aggregation by selection frequency. The function and the former components are preserved for compatibility, without attributing formal error control to the procedure.
  • The documentation distinguishes the residual Gaussian criterion from a node-by-node pseudo-likelihood or a composite likelihood.

mcglmgraph 0.2.0

Fixes

  • The residual layer explicitly requests residuals(..., type = "pearson"); the previous call received the default raw residuals of mcglm.
  • The ordering argument of the DAG layer is now applied by a consistent permutation of the responses, the edges and the fitted matrices.
  • The GGM line search keeps the last admissible iteration when it fails to find a positive definite proposal.
  • The PC-stable skeleton examines the frozen neighborhoods of both endpoints of each edge. On the optional route, a blacklist prevents bnlearn from adding edges outside the skeleton; since score-based search can remove edges, that route is not described as the orientation of a fixed skeleton.
  • The documentation distinguishes the methods inherited from the first-stage mcglm fit from the specific results stored in the $graph component.

This release aligns the estimators with the MCGLM-Graph method.

Estimation changes

  • DAG layer: the Newton step for the innovation variances now operates on the unconstrained reparametrization xi = log(delta), with delta = exp(xi). Positive definiteness of Sigma_b is guaranteed by construction for any (gamma, xi), dispensing with the hard projection pmax(delta, eps) that introduced a non-differentiable update at the boundary. The estimating function and the sensitivity are mapped to the xi scale by the diagonal Jacobian d(delta)/d(xi) = diag(delta), and the reported inference remains on the interpretable (gamma, delta) scale.

Documentation

  • In the user-facing interpretations, “conditional independence” was replaced by “second-order conditional association”, which coincides with full conditional independence under joint normality. In Gaussian copula models the graphical interpretation belongs to the latent scale (mc_partial_cor, mc_test_independence, package overview).
  • mc_test_independence: title and label of the test updated to “conditional association”.
  • CPDAG partial-correlation test: recorded the caveat that Fisher’s z transformation is a working approximation under non-Gaussian families, with the Wald/delta-method route as a robust alternative.
